verdict.justification: Both deliverables identify the same correct core results: 48 June-shipped POs, $140,008.20 shipped at cost, $5,210.60 short-shipped, and five June-window POs totaling $13,300.00 that shipped in July. B better satisfies the account-filtering requirement because its summary totals use SUBTOTAL, whereas A's summary totals use SUM and therefore do not adjust when account rows are filtered. B also presents a more compact second summary containing only affected accounts, rather than A's seven-account table with zero-activity rows. Its commentary directly quantifies the shipment-dollar impact—“June shipments would have been about $153,256.20”—which is especially relevant to the requested monthly shipped-value recap, while A emphasizes the counterfactual order value instead. A preserves source precision more faithfully and has useful timing notes, but B's clearer front-page structure and filter-responsive summaries make it the more usable account-management deliverable.

decisive_issues.issue: Main summary totals do not recalculate for filtered account rows.
Provides filter-responsive shipped-dollar totals directly in the summary.
Explains July slippage in terms of the actual shipment-dollar impact.
decisive_issues.quote: Had they shipped on time, June shipments would have been about $153,256.20
